response:
I recovered all 11 records and wrote them to `/app/recovered.json`, sorted by id.

**What was wrong:** every byte of the WAL file had been XORed with `0x42`. The giveaway was the long runs of `B` (0x42) where the zero padding should be. I reversed the XOR and wrote the result back to `/app/main.db-wal`. After that, SQLite reads the WAL normally and `items` returns 11 rows instead of 5. I copied the original `main.db` and `main.db-wal` to `/tmp/bak/` inside the container before changing anything.

**Recovered data:**

| id | name | value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | apple | 150 |
| 2 | banana | 250 |
| 3 | cherry | 300 |
| 4 | date | 400 |
| 5 | elderberry | 500 |
| 6 | fig | 600 |
| 7 | grape | 700 |
| 8 | honeydew | 800 |
| 9 | kiwi | 900 |
| 10 | lemon | 1000 |
| 11 | mango | 1100 |

Rows 6–11 came from the WAL. Apple (150) and banana (250) don't follow the pattern of the other values, so the WAL probably also updated those two rows from the base data. The JSON has these final values.
